I am a 46-year-old woman farming in the North West, and this small plot of beans is intercropped with my millet. Because beans can draw nitrogen from the air, I will not waste the little inorganic fertilizer I can access on this plot—I will save it for the cereal crops that need it more. I will, however, spread manure from our few animals on this plot since it is close to the compound, and I must spray some pesticide because cowpea pod borer destroys the harvest if left alone. My children and I will do most of the work ourselves, but I may hire a few extra hands when the weeding and harvest come.
